questions.question: What does it mean for $\lambda$ to be a root of $p(x)$?
What is another common name for a root of a polynomial?
Where must a root $\lambda$ of $p\in\mathbb F[x]$ live?
options: In every possible field at once
In the field $\mathbb F$ under discussion

questions.question: Why is a root described as an input rather than as a coefficient?
options: Because it is never a scalar
Because it is always the constant term
Because it must multiply the leading coefficient
Because it is substituted into the polynomial

questions.question: What does it mean to say a field is algebraically closed?
options: Every polynomial over it is constant, in every case without exception.
Every nonconstant polynomial over it has a root in that field
Every element of the field is zero

questions.question: Which number is a root of $p(x)=x-2$?
Which are the roots of $p(x)=x^2-1$?
Is $3$ a root of $p(x)=x^2-9$?
options: No, because roots must be negative

questions.question: Which candidate is not a root of $x^2-1$?
For $p(x)=x^2+1$ over $\mathbb R$, is $i$ a root in the sense of roots in $\mathbb R$?
options: Yes, because every polynomial has a real root

questions.question: How is a root of a polynomial related to a zero of a function?
options: Zeros must be complex but roots must be real
It is the same idea applied to the polynomial function
A root is a coefficient but a zero is an input
A root is the leading coefficient of the polynomial

questions.question: Why does the phrase “over $\mathbb F$” matter when asking for roots?
options: A candidate root must belong to the field being used
The coefficients are ignored once the field is named
The polynomial degree changes when the field is named
Every field has exactly the same roots for every polynomial

questions.question: What does a root reveal about divisibility by a linear factor, when polynomial division is available?
options: It means the polynomial is constant
It suggests that $x-\lambda$ divides the polynomial
It means $\lambda$ is the leading coefficient

questions.question: For $p(x)=x^3-8$, which number is a root?
For $p(x)=x^2-4x+4$, which statement about roots is correct?
If $p(5)=7$, what can be concluded about $5$?
options: The polynomial has no roots at all

questions.question: Why can a polynomial have no roots in one field but have roots in a larger field?
options: The allowed candidates depend on the field containing the scalars
The value $p(\lambda)$ is never affected by the input
Larger fields always change the polynomial coefficients to zero

questions.question: For a nonzero polynomial, roots are inputs giving zero. Why is the zero polynomial exceptional?
options: The zero polynomial has exactly one root, regardless of the specific input chosen.
Every scalar makes the zero polynomial evaluate to zero
The zero polynomial is not a polynomial
The zero polynomial has no input values

questions.question: Over $\mathbb R$, how many roots does $p(x)=x^2+1$ have?
If $p(x)=(x-1)^2(x+3)$, which statement is correct?
options: The polynomial has no roots because one factor is squared
